name: University of Oxford, Faculty of Law
tech_center: Deep Tech Dispute Resolution Lab; university Institute for Ethics in AI (joint Law/AI-regulation post)
highlights: Law and Computer Science option (BCL/MJur) co-taught with the CS department: mixed law/CS teams design and implement a digital legal service as a group project
Grew out of the Oxford Lawtech Education Programme piloted with Slaughter and May
Deep Tech Dispute Resolution Lab prototypes ODR/smart-contract tech with legal designers and engineers
Extensive AI-and-law research around the Institute for Ethics in AI
caveats: Undergraduate degree remains predominantly doctrinal; the Deep Tech lab's current activity level is uncertain after its founding director moved institutions.

name: University of Cambridge, Faculty of Law
highlights: LLM paper 'Law, Technology and Society' explicitly covers AI and machine learning, alongside strong IP/information-law papers via CIPIL
Cambridge hosts Hack_the_Law / LLM x Law Hackathon (King's Entrepreneurship Lab): 2025 edition drew students from 43 universities, with winners fast-tracked into the SPARK incubator
caveats: The hackathon is hosted by King's College's Entrepreneurship Lab, not the Law Faculty; no faculty tech center, clinic, or legal-tech degree.

name: University College London (UCL), Faculty of Laws
tech_center: Institute of Brand and Innovation Law; Information Technology Law Collective
highlights: New LLM Law and Technology specialism (2026-27): AI and algorithmic decision-making, data governance, platform regulation, fintech, digital-markets competition
AI and Law summer school and 'AI for Lawyers' executive course for practitioners
Research community that shapes courts, regulators, and governments on digital technology law
caveats: Taught academic pathway — no clinic where students build or deploy legal tech.

name: King's College London (Dickson Poon School of Law)
tech_center: Centre for Technology, Ethics, Law and Society (TELOS)
highlights: World-first AI Literacy Programme (Jan 2026): every law student and staff member gets free access to Harvey, Legora, Luminance, and Lucio AI with structured training
King's Legal Clinic integrates legal AI (Legora) into live clinical casework — students deploy AI in real access-to-justice work
LLM pathways in Law & Technology and Digital Law (online option); AI Governance module taught by Luminance's general counsel
Freshfields sponsors a fully funded tech-focused LLM at King's for its future trainees

name: Swansea University (Hillary Rodham Clinton School of Law)
tech_center: Legal Innovation Lab Wales (£5.6m facility with an in-house software team and legal AI laboratory)
highlights: LLM in LegalTech and Commercial Law with compulsory modules on AI in legal practice and blockchain/e-transactions regulation
A funded lab with actual software developers on staff, building tools for legal businesses, access to justice, and security platforms
Law Clinic connected to the lab, so LegalTech tools are developed and applied in clinic work
Open collaboration model with law firms, technology companies, and security organisations

name: Bucerius Law School
tech_center: Center for Legal Technology and Data Science (academic director: Daniel Martin Katz)
highlights: Flagship 3-week summer program 'AI, Legal Technology and Operations' with a hackathon capstone — instructors drawn from industry, Stanford CodeX, and the Legal Design Lab
Legal Technology and Operations specialization in the Master of Law and Business; Technology Certificate within the LLB
Legal Data Science Research Group and BMBF-funded NLP research (HILANO); publishes legal tech market and legal-ops reports with industry
Widely regarded as continental Europe's leading legal-tech law school hub

name: IE University — IE Law School
tech_center: LawAhead Center; Lawtomation Centre (Jean Monnet Centre of Excellence); IE Legaltech Innovation Farm
highlights: Master in Legaltech (ML, legalbots, blockchain, cybersecurity, big data) plus an AI-Powered Legal Practice program covering the EU AI Act and AI governance
Legaltech Innovation Farm — Spain's first legaltech open-innovation ecosystem, co-developing solutions with Santander, A&O, Baker McKenzie, Deloitte, Linklaters, IBM, and Microsoft
Runs the Global LegalTech Venture Days international startup competition with the Law Schools Global League
AI embedded across curricula 'from Digital Law to AI-Powered Legal Practice'

name: Tilburg University — Tilburg Law School
tech_center: Tilburg Institute for Law, Technology, and Society (TILT)
highlights: TILT is one of Europe's top law-and-technology research institutes; edits the journal Technology and Regulation and hosts TILTing Perspectives
LLM Law and Technology (English, two intakes/year, on-campus or fully online) spanning AI governance, privacy, cybercrime, fintech, and platform regulation
Lawyers from international firms are systematically involved in LLM teaching
caveats: Regulation-focused rather than build-focused — no student software-building clinic identified.

name: Maastricht University — Faculty of Law
tech_center: Maastricht Law & Tech Lab; European Centre on Privacy and Cybersecurity
highlights: Genuinely build-oriented lab: open-source legal NLP models on Hugging Face, case-law network software, and public GitHub repos ('maastrichtlawtech')
LLM Law & AI specialisation, Advanced Master in Privacy/Cybersecurity/Data Management, Bachelor Minor in Law and Technology, Legal Analytics course, and a Python Club for law students
Rethinking Justice 24-hour hackathon with students, staff, alumni, and industry
Problem-Based Learning pedagogy faculty-wide

name: University of Helsinki — Faculty of Law
tech_center: Legal Tech Lab (director Riikka Koulu, professor of Social and Legal Implications of AI)
highlights: Nordic pioneer: organized Finland's first legal hackathon (2017) and hosts the Legal Tech Con conference
Strong critical/academic scholarship on algorithmic decision-making and AI in judicial processes
caveats: Much documented student-facing activity dates from 2017-2018; current intensity of programming is uncertain. No specialized legal-tech degree.

name: University of Copenhagen — Faculty of Law
tech_center: Copenhagen Legal/Tech Lab; Centre for Information and Innovation Law (CIIR)
highlights: Hands-on courses: Legal Tech Laboratory (working with deployed European legal-tech tools), DigiLawyer, How to Start a Start-up (with real Copenhagen startups)
Campus Legal/Tech Hackathons ('Decentralising Finance' 2022, 'AI for a Sustainable Future' 2023) with industry mentors
Lab maps the Danish legal-tech ecosystem (Legal Tech Map & Report 2024); CIIR researches generative AI and IP
caveats: The lab's funded project appears wound down (community activities continue); no specialized legal-tech degree.

name: University of Geneva — Faculty of Law
highlights: Certificat en droit du numérique (from 2025) with a mandatory Digital and AI Law course and workshop, capped at 25 students
Annual Digital Law Summer School (AI, cybersecurity, big data, platform law) with an embedded clinic experience
Collaborations with Berkman Klein, ITU, WIPO, and Geneva's international-organization ecosystem
caveats: Strength is regulatory scholarship and the IO ecosystem rather than students building technology.

name: University of St. Gallen (HSG) — Law School
tech_center: Law & Tech Lab @ HSG (six-professor research cluster)
highlights: Optional Law and Technology specialization within the MLaw, Master in Law and Economics, and Master in International Law
Active faculty output on AI liability, algorithmic decision-making, robotics, and platform regulation (Wildhaber, Simmler, Buiten, Tamò-Larrieux)
First 'Hack the Law' legal hackathon scheduled November 2026; Swiss LegalTech Association student chapter bridges to industry
HSG's integrative law-plus-management model

name: University of Edinburgh — Edinburgh Law School
tech_center: SCRIPT Centre (Scottish Research Centre for IP and Technology Law)
highlights: One of Europe's deepest and most technical tech-law catalogues: Robotics AI and the Law, Software and the Law, Hardware and the Law, Decentralised Technologies, Cybercrime and Cyber Security
LLM in Innovation, Technology and the Law (on-campus and online) plus an online LLM in IT Law
Law and AI Hackathon where student teams build tech solutions; Summer School in Legal Technology with international practitioners
Burkhard Schafer's computational legal theory group is among the longest-established in Europe

name: Queen Mary University of London (CCLS)
tech_center: Technology, Media and Telecommunications Law Institute (CCLS); qLegal
highlights: Dedicated LLM and PGCert in AI and the Law (Comparative and International AI Law, Competition and AI, Dispute Resolution and AI) alongside the long-running TMT LLM (online since 2003)
qLegal: award-winning clinic where postgraduate students advise real tech startups; externships embed students in startups one day/week for six months
Future of Law Programme: interdisciplinary law + CS teams prototype chatbots, apps, and legal design solutions (Enterprise Nation hackathon)
Faculty advise governments on AI regulation; UK's largest LLM programme

name: KU Leuven — Faculty of Law and Criminology
tech_center: CiTiP — Centre for IT & IP Law (80+ researchers; imec research group)
highlights: Continental Europe's research powerhouse for IT/IP law: heavy involvement in EU digital regulation scholarship (GDPR, AI Act, cybersecurity) via dozens of EU projects
Advanced Master (LLM) of Intellectual Property and ICT Law in Brussels, taught partly by European Commission officials and regulators
Unmatched engineering integration via imec, LICT, COSIC, and DistriNet; annual Leuven IP and AI Conference
caveats: Student opportunities to build legal tech are thinner than at QMUL or Edinburgh; no tech-build clinic.
